answer: The basalt test I would run is Bond in a volatile asset the attacker cannot hedge cheaply: a bond in an asset that swings twenty percent a week, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Each account presents its proof once, the network verifies it in seconds, and a farm that wants ten accounts must pass ten independent checks — the pulse is that the work cannot be shared or replayed. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the canyon of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
